question: An object is placed in front of a concave mirror at a point between its pole P and focus F. The image formed is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**virtual and erect.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave mirror creates an erect and virtual image when an object is positioned between its focus and pole.**
 
• The image is **virtual because the reflected rays do not actually converge at the position** where the image appears to be located.
 
• The** image is erect because the object and the image are both on the same side of the mirror**, and the reflected rays do not cross over.
 
• The size of the image is larger than the size of the object, and the image appears to be located behind the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A convex mirror is also known as a diverging mirror as it diverges the light rays.
 
• The image formed by a convex mirror is always virtual, diminished, and upright.
 
• The principal focus of a convex mirror is a point on the principal axis where the light rays appear to diverge from after reflecting from the mirror.
 
• The focal length of a convex mirror is always negative, and it is equal to half of the radius of curvature of the mirror.
